newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: APEC likely to back drive to free up computer trade.
newsitem.headline: APEC likely to back drive to free up computer trade.

text.p: MANILA, Philippines - Asia-Pacific countries are likely to back a U.S. proposal to drop tariffs on computers and computer-related products by the start of the 21st century, officials said Thursday.

A draft statement to be issued by ministers from the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum during the group's meetings this week in Manila welcomed the Information Technology Agreement pushed by the United States.

"Ministers agreed that the information technology sector is an important sector of world trade," the statement said, adding they hoped it "would mark another milestone in multilateral trade liberalisation efforts."
The United States has proposed zero tariffs on a wide range of computer and computer-related products within APEC and other economies by the year 2000.
Washington wants APEC's support on the information technology agreement before putting it on the table at the inaugural meeting of the World Trade Organisation next month in Singapore.
The draft statement indicated that APEC trade and foreign ministers would recommend that their leaders endorse the U.S. proposal when they meet Monday for their summit.
The ministers begin two days of meetings Friday ahead of Monday's summit at Subic Bay, north of the capital.
U.S. Undersecretary of State Joan Spero said a broad consensus had been reached about the agreement, although details still had to be worked out.
Other U.S. officials said they were still working to include the formula of zero tariffs on computer and telecommunications by the year 2000 in the vaguely worded APEC draft statement.
The United States currently accounts for 60 percent of world trade in information technology products.
Spero said trade in information technology was a $1.8 trillion business.

Philippine Foreign Affairs Undersecretary Federico Macaranas has said that some of the economies in the Asia-Pacific area, the world's most dynamic region, fear the agreement would benefit only a few countries, such as major software exporters like the United States.
Spero said APEC was likely to express its support for the agreement, although China reportedly opposes it.

"APEC operates very much on a consensus. One country doesn't have to sign on. ... But it's very hard for that country to block it when there's a broad consensus and when that country isn't part of the WTO," she said.

APEC groups China, Taiwan, the United States, Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Korea, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Thailand and Singapore. Of these, only China and Taiwan are not members of the WTO.
